anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved f5 to holds by explicitly selecting the "expired deadline" row, running the Wait-course expiry check before any poll, refusing renewal from either retained grant or expiry, keeping poll_deadline at 12:15:00Z, and surfacing the expiry in the rendered wait row ("since the last window expired at 12:15:00Z"). Before noted the elapsed window in narration and did not re-poll or renew, but it folded the expiry into an ordinary Pending-row render: the verdict, comments block and wait row read as a plain pending-check menu with no timeout obstacle presented to the reader, so a careful reader could not say the expired deadline yielded a timeout obstacle. To make this more robust in After, consider naming the obstacle in the rendered report itself (e.g. a line under PR comments or the verdict such as "poll window expired at 12:15:00Z; a new wait selection is required") rather than only in the wait row's description, so the obstacle is visible even if the row text is later shortened; the narration's expiry-check-before-poll and no-renewal statements should stay as written.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After explicitly records the expired-window obstacle in the continuation record, surfaces it in the report ('The verification wait window expired, so further polling requires a new wait selection'), states that neither retained grant renews the deadline, runs no polling or sleep, and makes the recommended wait item an explicit new 15-minute window pick — that is exactly what moved f5 from fails to holds. Before only noted the expiry in its internal narration and then quietly resolved the window to Pending without recording or reporting any timeout obstacle, and its menu offered a generic 'wait - poll the binding check' that reads as plain resumption rather than a renewed window, so a careful reader could not say a timeout obstacle was yielded. Keep the After wording: the obstacle-recording sentence in step 2, the dedicated expired-window comment line, and the 'start a new 15-minute window' phrasing on the wait item together deliver the Change (bounded, selection-gated waiting with retained grants) while making the no-automatic-renewal behaviour visible in the rendered output rather than only in the narration.
